capital: Memphis (Old Kingdom name Inbu-hedj, "White Walls"; Men-nefer is the later name derived from Pepi I's pyramid town)

sources.title: Shaw, Ian (ed.), The Oxford History of Ancient Egypt, Oxford University Press, 2000 — esp. Jaromír Málek, 'The Old Kingdom (c. 2686-2160 BC)'. Chronological framework used for year_start/year_end.

Hornung, Erik; Krauss, Rolf; Warburton, David A. (eds.), Ancient Egyptian Chronology, Handbook of Oriental Studies I/83, Brill, Leiden, 2006 — chronological tables pp. 490-495 (Dynasty 3 from c. 2592, end of Old Kingdom c. 2150/2118 BCE).

Wilkinson, Toby A. H., Royal Annals of Ancient Egypt: The Palermo Stone and its Associated Fragments, Kegan Paul International, London, 2000 — edition and translation of the Palermo Stone, the primary source for Sneferu's Nubian (7,000 captives, 200,000 cattle) and Libyan raids.

Lehner, Mark, 'Labor and the Pyramids: The Heit el-Ghurab "Workers Town" at Giza', in Steinkeller & Hudson (eds.), Labor in the Ancient World, ISLET, 2015 — archaeological evidence for corvée-conscripted (not enslaved) pyramid labor.

Hawass, Zahi & Lehner, Mark, 'Builders of the Pyramids', Archaeology 50/1, 1997, pp. 30-38 — builders' cemetery and workers' settlement at Giza; Egyptian-led excavation (non-Western historiography: Hawass, Egyptian Supreme Council of Antiquities).

Moeller, Nadine, 'The First Intermediate Period: A Time of Famine and Climate Change?', Ägypten und Levante / Egypt and the Levant 15, 2005, pp. 153-167 — critique of climate monocausality for the Old Kingdom collapse.

provenance: AtlasPI metadata; bibliography supplied by its editors. Not independently audited.
